RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination on its own — it's common in sectors where leadership is male-dominated, and it proves nothing about intent. Raise it only as background context, never as your main argument.

Your strong point is the qualification comparison: a master's in educational leadership plus five years actually doing the deputy's job against "courses" and classroom years only. In most equality frameworks, showing you were at least as qualified as the man appointed is what shifts the burden onto the employer to justify its choice. The unanswered request for written reasons strengthens that considerably.

Send a written follow-up citing your legal right to reasons, with a deadline. Keep the panel's composition in reserve.
